title: Armored Dino Found in Japan May Have Walked from Alaska!
summary:
Imagine a dinosaur wearing a suit of bony armor, stomping along a beach 100 million years ago. It walks and walks — all the way from what is now Alaska to what is now Japan. That's the story scientists think they've uncovered.

The dinosaur bones were dug up in Japan in 1995. For 30 years, nobody knew they belonged to a brand-new species. Now, after CT scans (special X-rays that let you see inside a fossil without breaking it), scientists have named it Nipponopelta yezoensis. 'Nippon' means Japan, and 'pelta' means 'shield' in Greek.

This dino was a nodosaurid — a plant-eater with bony plates on its back. It didn't have a tail club like its cousin the ankylosaurid. Only three nodosaurid species have ever been found in Asia, so this is a big deal.

How did it get there? Scientists think its ancestors crossed the Bering Land Bridge, a strip of land that once connected Alaska and Russia. The dinosaur probably followed the coast, munching plants the whole way. Its body may have washed out to sea after it died and sank to the ocean floor — which is where its fossils were found. Pretty cool for a dinosaur that's been waiting millions of years to say hello!
why_it_matters: It shows that the ground under our feet was once full of animals on the move, and that a box of bones sitting in a drawer for 30 years can still become an amazing discovery.

background_read: Alaska (the big state in the far north of the USA) and Russia are separated by cold sea today, but long ago a strip of land called the Bering Land Bridge joined them.
Animals — and even early humans — walked across that bridge to move between continents, so scientists think dinosaurs could have travelled the same way.
Nodosaurids are a family of armored plant-eating dinosaurs whose fossils are usually found in North America and Europe, which is why finding one in Asia is such a rare event.
Article_Structure: WHO: Scientists who studied old dinosaur bones dug up in Japan in 1995 and gave the new species the name Nipponopelta yezoensis.
WHAT: They announced a brand-new armored dinosaur — a nodosaurid plant-eater with bony plates on its back but no tail club — after using CT scans to see inside the fossil.

WHERE: The fossils came from Japan, but the scientists think the dinosaur's ancestors walked from Alaska across the Bering Land Bridge, and that its body later washed out to sea and sank to the ocean floor.
WHY: Only three nodosaurid species have ever been found in Asia, so this find helps show how dinosaurs spread from one continent to another.

perspectives.description: Researchers are thrilled because a new species was hiding in plain sight for 30 years, and because it is only the third nodosaurid ever found in Asia.
Some experts may say the idea that the dinosaur walked all the way from Alaska to Japan is only a theory — the bones alone cannot prove the exact route it took.
People who love dinosaurs get a new name to learn, plus a cool story about ancient animals trekking across a land bridge between continents.
